newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil remains firmly higher pre-close.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil remains firmly higher pre-close.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil retained its sharp gains near the market's close Friday buoyed by a strong finish by gas oil futures on London's IPE, and crude oil prices gained momentum to make session highs.
"It could still run up since there is a lot of buying interest," said a trader of heating oil's price rise.
October heating oil, which has followed gas oil futures in London higher since the session's start, stood 1.47 cents higher at 66.50 cents a gallon.
September gas oil settled $7 higher at $219.75 cents a tonne on the IPE Friday, 75 cents of the day's high.
October crude rose to a session high, up 33 cents to $23.77 a barrel.

Traders attributed the rise to short covering ahead of the weekend. They said crude oil's uptrend is expected to continue after staying firmly above $23.00 following its sharp gains Tuesday on the Iraqi conflict.
"The market has absorbed the news from Tuesday, and now there is a new leadership of the longs," said a trader.
Dealers said crude prices were also boosted by gains in heat which inspired gains in gasoline as well. October gasoline was up 0.59 cent to 65.00 cents a gallon.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, +1 212-859-1761.
